title: Records and Mr. Peer of OKeh
summary: Asked about Russ Papalia on his records, he says nothing distinguished his records and begins a story about OKeh's Mr. Peer and a golf game.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I was wondering about your records and Russ Papalia. He played trouble with me on the records.

But I would say here and now there is nothing of distinction attached to my records. I made a terrible mistake. A man came down here. No, I had a friend, Mr. Peer. He was a man that was doing his own piano house. And he was friendly with, no, I'm going to get the names all wrong. Mr. Peer was the president of OK Records. He played a fair golf game. And he played a fair golf game. But he thought he played a better one. So I let him win the second nine. First thing your secretary says, Mr. Peer beat you on the second nine. I said, let me touch him. I'm going to beat him with one o'clock. We used to have to cross the river, go under the tunnel, get a trolley car, jump on a steam train. I don't know where we went to play golf around New York. I'm talking about New York.
Yeah. But he liked me. He made my kid.
